To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the parallel concatenation approach, which is already successfully used in turbo filtering, can be extended to the development of smoothing methods; and (ii) turbo smoothing can outperform the state of the art in smoothing techniques.

(a) the turbo filtering concept can be exploited to develop a new smoothing method called turbo smoothing and (b) the proposed smoothing technique is capable of achieving better complexity-accuracy performance than other recently proposed smoothing techniques.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the derivation of a new smoothing method based on a parallel concatenation of filters.
the development of novel algorithms, based on a new theoretical framework, that are capable of improving the accuracy/performance of existing filtering/smoothing methods.
the development of new algorithms, based on a parallel concatenation of filters, for the smoothing problem in dynamic systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
turbo filtering and smoothing are new, powerful tools for developing filtering algorithms with improved complexity-accuracy tradeoffs.

the new proposed smoothing technique, based on the turbo principle, is able to improve the performance in the presence of high measurement noise, with respect to the classical Kalman smoother, while preserving a complexity comparable to the classical Kalmansmoothers.
the new smoothing method is able to achieve the best complexity-accuracy trade-off among all the smoothing techniques available in the literature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
turbo smoothing is a new and promising technique that can be used to design smoothing algorithms for nonlinear/non-Gaussian state-space models.

, by exploiting the same conceptual approach, we can devise a turbo smoothing method that, as the turbo filter, is able to provide a better complexity-accuray tradeoff than other filtering algorithms.
turbo smoothing is a novel and effective smoothing technique that, in some situations, can be used as an alternative to the classical forward/backward filtering/smoothing algorithms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the parallel concatenation approach, originally developed for turbo filtering, can also be successfully applied for turbo smoothing.
the turbo filtering approach is not restricted to filtering but can be extended to smoothing.
turbo smoothing, as well as turbo filtering, can be regarded as a novel paradigm for designing efficient recursive algorithms for nonlinear filtering and smoothing.
